# swarmops land

Merge a change three-way onto a ref and publish it there as one new changeset.

The change is HEAD with its first-parent chain since the base, squashed: the new changeset's parent is the ref's head, it holds what the chain changed merged with what the ref gained since the base, and the ref moves to it in the same transaction. A ref that moves meanwhile makes the land merge again onto its new head and retry, up to --max-attempts times. A conflict is E\_CONFLICT (exit 3), with each conflicting file in details.report, and nothing is recorded; land again with --resolve to resolve it without a checkout.

```yaml
title: "swarmops land"
description: "Merge a change three-way onto a ref and publish it there as one new changeset."
group: "write"
since: "0.1.0"
mutates: true
identity_required: true
mcp_tool: "land"
envelope_op: "land"
exit_codes: [0, 1, 3]
errors: [E_CONFLICT, E_NOTHING_TO_LAND]
syntax: "swarmops land [OPTIONS] <HEAD>"
```

## Syntax

```text
swarmops land [OPTIONS] <HEAD>
```

## Required arguments

### `HEAD`

Syntax: `<HEAD>`.

The changeset to land: the change's head, such as the changeset a commit made.

## Optional arguments

The command also takes the [global options](../cli.md#global-options).

### `--base`

Syntax: `--base <REV>`.

Where the change starts: a first-parent ancestor of HEAD, whose own changes are not landed (default: the merge base of HEAD and the ref's head, along first parents).

### `--target`

Syntax: `--target <REF>`.
Default: `main`.

The ref to land on: main or release/&lt;name&gt;.

### `--message`

Syntax: `-m, --message <MSG>`.

The new changeset's message (default: HEAD's).

### `--key`

Syntax: `--key <KEY>`.

Makes a retry of this land safe: 1 to 64 letters, digits and '-', such as a uuid v7. Make a new one for each change you land, and give it again only to retry that land.

A land with a key first looks down the ref's first parents, to the change's base, for a changeset landed with the same key: one squashed from this HEAD is the land made before, which the land replays (status: replayed) without writing anything; one from another head is E\_INVALID\_ARG. Without a key, the same land run again finds its change on the ref already: E\_NOTHING\_TO\_LAND.

### `--max-attempts`

Syntax: `--max-attempts <N>`.
Default: `8`.

How many times to try to publish before E\_CAS\_RETRY\_EXHAUSTED: 1 to 32.

### `--max-conflict-bytes`

Syntax: `--max-conflict-bytes <N>`.
Default: `32768`.

The most bytes of hunk text an E\_CONFLICT report carries; past them it leaves the texts out (truncated) and keeps every line position and blob id.

### `--resolve`

Syntax: `--resolve <FILE>`.

Resolve the conflicts an E\_CONFLICT report named, without a checkout: resolutions as a JSON object in FILE, or - for stdin, at most 64 MiB (swarmops schema ResolutionsInput).

{"against": THEIRS, "files": {PATH: RESOLUTION, ...}}: THEIRS is the report's theirs, by its full id, and each RESOLUTION one of {"take": "ours"}, {"take": "theirs"}, {"content": CONTENT} with an optional "mode" (CONTENT as a commit's change gives it: inline, base64, a file, or a stored blob by id) and {"delete": true}. A resolution decides its path and every path below it; the rest of the merge stands.

A resolution applies while the ref holds its path as THEIRS did, whether the path conflicts or not. A path the ref changed since is stale: the land fails with E\_CONFLICT again, its report naming the path in stale, as it does for each conflict left unresolved. Read the report's theirs, and resolve against it.

## Examples

### CLI

```sh
swarmops --repo [tmp]/store --as agent/worker-17 land [head] --key land-7
```

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "op": "land",
  "api": 1,
  "result": {
    "status": "landed",
    "landed": "[landed]",
    "rebased_onto": "[theirs]",
    "target": "main",
    "base": "[t0]",
    "attempts": 1,
    "relocated": false,
    "files_changed": 1,
    "squashed_from": [
      "[head]"
    ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "repo": "[tmp]/store",
    "elapsed_ms": "[elapsed_ms]",
    "resolved": {
      "[head]": "[head]",
      "main": "[theirs]"
    },
    "auth": "trust"
  }
}
```

Exit code 0. Recorded by the CLI tests. A name in square brackets, such as `[tmp]` or `[c1]`, stands for what differs from run to run: the test's temporary directory, an id, a time.

## Return information

`result` is a `LandResp` (`swarmops schema LandResp` prints its JSON Schema).

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `attempts` | `integer` | yes | How many times the land tried to publish. |
| `auto_merged` | `array of string` | no | The paths both sides changed that merged cleanly. Omitted when empty. |
| `base` | `string` | yes | The changeset the change was taken from: what `head`'s first-parent chain added after it is what landed. |
| `files_changed` | `integer` | yes | How many paths the landed changeset changes. |
| `landed` | `string` | yes | The landed changeset: the change squashed into one changeset on the target. |
| `rebased_onto` | `string` | yes | The target's head the change landed on: `landed`'s parent. |
| `relocated` | `boolean` | yes | The target moved after the land read it, and the publish put the change on the new head itself, without another attempt. |
| `squashed_from` | `array of string` | yes | The changesets the land squashed, oldest first: `head`'s first-parent chain after `base`, ending at `head`. |
| `status` | `LandStatus` | yes | `landed`, or `replayed` when a land with the same `idempotency_key` had landed the change already. |
| `target` | `string` | yes | The ref it landed on. |
| `warnings` | `array of string` | no | Problems found after the land became durable, such as failed housekeeping; the land itself succeeded. Omitted when empty. |

Envelope `op`: `land`.

Exit codes:

- `0`: Success.
- `1`: The operation failed.
- `3`: The change conflicts with what it lands on: resolve it, then run the operation again.

## Errors

- [`E_CONFLICT`](../errors.md#e_conflict) (exit 3): The change conflicts with the target: `details.report` lists each conflicting file with its kind, its hunks and who changed it on the target.
- [`E_NOTHING_TO_LAND`](../errors.md#e_nothing_to_land) (exit 1): The land has nothing to add to the target: its head is on the target already, or its change is (`details.reason` says which).

Any command that opens a store may also fail with a store error, such as [`E_NOT_A_REPO`](../errors.md#e_not_a_repo), [`E_IO`](../errors.md#e_io) or [`E_STORE_CORRUPT`](../errors.md#e_store_corrupt); a command line the grammar refuses is [`E_INVALID_ARG`](../errors.md#e_invalid_arg) (exit 2).
